definitions.explanation: A formal term referring to a married couple, often used when speaking about others respectfully.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}{夫妻|ふさい}に{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met Mr. and Mrs. Tanaka.

examples.japanese: あの{夫妻|ふさい}は{仲|なか}がいい。
examples.english: That married couple gets along well.

examples.japanese: {山田|やまだ}{夫妻|ふさい}をパーティーに{招待|しょうたい}した。
examples.english: I invited Mr. and Mrs. Yamada to the party.

examples.japanese: {鈴木|すずき}{夫妻|ふさい}は{来月|らいげつ}{結婚|けっこん}30{周年|しゅうねん}を{迎|むか}える。
examples.english: Mr. and Mrs. Suzuki will celebrate their 30th wedding anniversary next month.

examples.japanese: その{夫妻|ふさい}は{世界|せかい}{各地|かくち}を{旅行|りょこう}するのが{好|す}きだそうだ。
examples.english: I hear that couple likes to travel around the world.

notes:
{夫妻|ふさい} is a formal way to refer to a married couple, typically used when speaking about others (not oneself).

Usage:
- [surname]{夫妻|ふさい} - Mr. and Mrs. [surname]
- Often used in formal contexts, news, or when showing respect

Related terms:
- {夫婦|ふうふ} (husband and wife - more common, can refer to one's own marriage)
- ご{夫婦|ふうふ} (married couple - polite)
- カップル (couple - loanword, not necessarily married)

Difference:
- {夫妻|ふさい} - used for others, more formal
- {夫婦|ふうふ} - more general, can be used for self or others
